subject: Post-call: cloud buying lanes & procurement readiness — PO timing vs marketplace paths
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@novushealth.com>, John Lee <john.lee@novushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: cloud buying lanes & procurement readiness

Hi Samantha / John —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + suggested next steps so we keep momentum with procurement: 

What we heard (Novus needs):
- Primary preference: predictable commercial terms and SOC2-backed controls for PHI-adjacent workloads.
- Procurement options under consideration: 1) Direct PO (standard SOW + invoicing), 2) AWS Marketplace (Private Offer) to leverage your internal buy-side team, 3) Corporate card for pilot/POC.
- Timeline signal: procurement estimates they can issue a PO in ~4–6 weeks if SOW/price is finalized; Private Offer could shorten internal approvals but needs marketplace onboarding and reseller paperwork.

Clarifying questions from our side:
1) Is short-term pilot acceptable on card while procurement processes Private Offer / PO for production?
2) Does Novus require a formal BAA / data processing addendum before a PO is issued?
3) Who on your procurement team should we include for a PO timeline and vendor setup (contact + email)?

Suggested next steps:
- I can share a one-page comparison (Marketplace Private Offer vs Direct PO) and a procurement checklist tailored to Novus — attaching both.
- If helpful, Marissa (enablement) or Ben (billing ops) can join a 30-min call with your procurement rep to walk the paperwork and timelines.

Proposed owners:
- Karthik: provide comparison + proposed pricing band for pilot and production.
- Marissa: run enablement / onboarding checklist with your procurement.
- Ben: confirm invoicing & tax details (required for PO).

If the above looks right, propose a short follow-up (30 min) with your procurement contact this week or early next week.

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: Redwood_Marketplace_vs_PO_2-pager.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: Procurement_Checklist_Novus.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@novushealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, John Lee <john.lee@novushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: cloud buying lanes & procurement readiness

Thanks Karthik — helpful recap. A few clarifications from Procurement side: 

- We prefer Marketplace Private Offer for new vendors when possible because it ties into our buy-side workflows and reduces manual vendor setup. That said, Private Offer onboarding requires our vendor team to confirm reseller details which can take 1–2 weeks to validate.
- For production (PHI-adjacent), Procurement will require a signed BAA and proof of SOC2 Type II; those are in scope before a PO is approved.
- Pilot: Corporate card for a 4–6 week pilot is acceptable if the dollar amount is under our threshold (we can confirm).

Action items from Novus: 
- I will introduce our procurement operations lead, John Lee (copied), who will coordinate vendor setup.
- Please send the marketplace seller profile and any reseller contacts you will use for a Private Offer.
- We need an example SOW and tax info for our legal team.

On timeline: if we get the paperwork together this week, John thinks vendor validation + Private Offer provisioning could happen in ~2 weeks; a formal PO for production likely 4–6 weeks thereafter.

Thanks — Samantha

Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: cloud buying lanes & procurement readiness

Looping Ben to confirm what we can provide quickly to accelerate Private Offer & PO:
- Ben: can we produce an AWS seller profile + reseller contact within 24 hours? Also confirm our standard tax/VAT form for Novus (US entity).
- Pricing: Karthik, suggest we offer a short-term pilot band that is card-friendly (low friction) and a production band that maps to a Private Offer discount if they commit to a 12-month reserved commit.

Ben — heads up: procurement will need SOC2 evidence and our BAA. I have the SOC2 report link and the BAA template — will share. Also recommend we proactively include a paragraph in the SOW about data residency controls to remove legal back-and-forth.

Quick internal asks:
- Ben: can you draft the vendor setup packet we send to Novus procurement (one page: what they need to create a Private Offer / accept invoices)?
- Karthik: once Ben confirms, I'll join the procurement intro call and walk through the checklist.

Thanks,
Marissa

--

Subject: Next steps & attachments: Marketplace vs PO, checklist, proposed timelines

Samantha / John —

Great — appreciate the clarity. Per our internal sync, attaching a concise packet and proposed timeline to help Procurement triage quickly: 

Attachments included:
- Redwood_Marketplace_vs_PO_2-pager.pdf — side-by-side of Private Offer, Direct PO, and card pilot tradeoffs.
- Procurement_Checklist_Novus.xlsx — vendor setup checklist (seller profile, reseller contact, tax forms, SOC2 link, BAA).

Key asks for Novus:
1) Please confirm whether Procurement wants us to route via AWS Marketplace Private Offer or proceed with direct vendor setup for PO. If Private Offer, please share the procurement contact who will raise the offer (we can provision the seller/reseller info).
2) If PO path: can you share the name/email of your AP contact and any required invoice fields so Ben can confirm format?
3) Target dates: pilot on card starting week of Jul 7? Full vendor setup / Private Offer live by Jul 1–14 to allow production PO by mid-July depending on legal review.

I will follow up with a 30-min scheduling link; Marissa will join the procurement call and Ben will own vendor setup items.

Thanks again — I’ll wait for John’s procurement contact and any questions.

Best,
Karthik
